subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: The coefficient
hotspots.description: The highlighted big number in front of each formula is the coefficient — it counts how many whole units of that substance react.
hotspots.positionHint: The large numbers at the front of each formula in the equation.
hotspots.function: Shows the number in front that counts units.

hotspots.label: It multiplies everything
hotspots.description: The coefficient multiplies every atom in the formula. When the count layer is on, 2H₂O expands into two full water molecules.
hotspots.positionHint: The formula expanding into real molecules when the count layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the coefficient multiplying every atom.

hotspots.label: The balanced result
hotspots.description: With the right coefficients, the atoms on the left exactly match the atoms on the right — the equation is balanced.
hotspots.positionHint: The matching atom tallies shown when the balance layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the equation balanced by the coefficients.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. A balanced chemical equation floats centered — 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O — with the coefficients emphasized, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Formulas are app-rendered glyphs on flat tiles; when the count layer expands them, they become clean ball-stick molecules (hydrogen warm off-white, oxygen muted red). Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots and the coefficient highlights (amber / molecular-green / coral accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Formula tiles: soft off-white matte, roughness ~0.6. Molecule spheres: CPK colors (H warm off-white, O muted red), roughness ~0.45-0.5. Bond rods: thin graphite cylinders. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: the equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, built to be read as 'the numbers in front count units and balance the reaction.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a flat equation scene — three formula tiles (app-rendered glyphs): LEFT `2H₂`, `O₂`; RIGHT `2H₂O`, with an arrow tile between. The coefficient glyphs (the 2s) are subtly raised/highlighted.

2) UNIT COUNT (toggleable layer): each formula expands into real ball-stick molecules — `2H₂` becomes two H₂ molecules, `O₂` one O₂, `2H₂O` two water molecules (app animates the expansion). The coefficient visually 'distributes' over the molecules.

3) BALANCE CHECK (toggleable layer): the expanded molecules split into their atoms and line up in two columns (reactants left, products right) with the same atoms mirrored — H count and O count match on both sides. App renders simple running tallies.

Camera: framed so the full equation fits with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 7-11k triangles. Named nodes: Tile_2H2, Tile_O2, Tile_2H2O, EquationArrow, Molecules_2H2, Molecule_O2, Molecules_2H2O, AtomColumns, Tallies. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
